question: Which confounding factors were considered, and how were they controlled for, for example by design, matching, stratification or adjustment?
Which statistical method was used to adjust for confounding?
Could participants switch between interventions during follow-up, and how was this handled?
How were participants selected into the study, and was their selection related to the intervention or the outcome?
Did follow-up start at the same time as the intervention for every participant?
How was intervention status defined and recorded, and was it known at the start of the intervention?
Were there deviations from the intended interventions or co-interventions, and did they differ between the groups?
How many participants had missing data on the outcome, the intervention or the confounders, and how was this handled?
How was the outcome measured, and were the assessors aware of the intervention received?
Was there a pre-registered protocol or analysis plan, and do the reported outcomes and analyses match it?
